background: UBS Group is Switzerland's only remaining global bank after absorbing Credit Suisse, the world's largest wealth manager, with Swiss retail and corporate banking, asset management and an investment bank, and a balance sheet far larger than the Swiss economy.
synthesis: Two of the three main agencies rate the group, A on average and the weakest of them at A-, both on a stable outlook, after a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 14 Apr 2026. Capital is solid on its own figures, with CET1 of 14.4% and leverage of 5.8%, and liquidity is ample, with LCR of 177% and NSFR of 115%; none of the ratios has moved materially over the past four periods. The pressure is regulatory rather than in the numbers: the newest flagged item, on 6 Oct 2026, is its exit from the fund-administration business inherited from Credit Suisse, and the rest centre on a Swiss capital plan that would force it to hold more capital or move abroad.
